issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the template declares the helper with no parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse()) while the problem statement UML and the reference solution declare it as singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Template: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 18 shows a parameter-less signature (the Animal parameter is commented out). Problem statement UML: problem_statement.md line 19 declares singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void. Reference solution: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 33 implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended method contract and prevents using the template verse implementation as-is, since the verse implementation and the UML expect an Animal parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.singFarmSongVerse signature to match the UML and the reference solution: change to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Inside the method use the provided parameter (animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()) so the template aligns with the specification while preserving the instructional TODOs elsewhere.
